fields.name: Actor
fields.evidence: bg3.exe+0x3312010 (called per entry of a HashMap<Guid, ...> of the timeline's actors from bg3.exe+0x3308CB0) creates the component (bg3.exe+0x3316120) on the actor's entity and copies the 16-byte map key here; the same key is passed as the actor Guid to the actor-data creation bg3.exe+0x330CEC0, and in the sibling branch it is stored after the timeline Guid of a request. Live: two different GUIDs for the two actors.

fields.name: field_10
fields.evidence: Copied with the array copy bg3.exe+0x2FBE710, whose element size is 4 (allocation count*4, 4-byte plain copies without reference counting - so not FixedString) from the first array of the component returned by bg3.exe+0x3311E10 for the timeline entity. bg3.exe+0x3308E10 treats the timeline as still waiting (keeps esv::ServerTimelineCreationConfirmationComponent) while any actor of that timeline has a non-empty array (size at +0x1C != 0). Live: pointer, capacity 1, size 1 on both instances. Most likely the users (UserId) that still have to confirm the actor, not proven.

fields.name: Timeline
fields.evidence: bg3.exe+0x3312010 stores the timeline entity (first field of the timeline query result) here; bg3.exe+0x3308E10 compares it with the timeline entity being checked. Live: the same entity handle on both instances.
